She did not turn, but only pulled her thin shawl tighter about her shoulders. "I'm watchin' the sun go down." "It's gone down already," he replied gently. "There's naught left but the colour it left behind. That aint the sun itself." She sighed, a little puff of white in the cool air. "It's something, aint it? A promise that it'll come back. "In a minute," she murmured, her gaze fixed on the fading violet streak at the world's edge. "I was just thinkin', Silas, of when mother was here, and the lamp would be lit by now, and the house would be full of the smell of supper. We won't never have that again, will we?" He had no answer for that. Her hand, small and cold, found its way into his. "Silas," she whispered, "leave me be for a bit." "Who'll see you safe inside?" "I'll see myself." He was the one solid post in a world where all the other fences had fallen down. Once inside, he went about lighting the lamp himself. It was the quiet that came before her spells of melancholy, a stillness that was more troubling than tears. "Clara," he said, kneeling to lay the kindling, "what do you think of a journey?" "But that's a good two days' ride." "I know it." "Why, Silas?" Her voice held a note of fretful alarm. "You don't like Aunby. You always said it was too crowded with folk." "It is not for me," he said, striking a match and touching it to the shavings. "It is for you. There is a doctor there, a good one, they say. And Cousin Mary's girls would be company for you." "I don't want company," she said, her head drooping. "I get tired of people. I only want you, Silas. You know I aint well except where you are." For it was so; her affliction of the nerves made her sharp and weary with others, but his presence was a balm she could not do without. "Would you rather stay here, then?" "Oh yes, Silas! oh yes!" He knew it with a heavy certainty that settled in his heart like a stone. "I saw Mr. Gable in town," Silas said, rising and turning to face her. "He asked about Father's old watch." Clara's breath caught. "The gold one?" "The very same." "But that was his pride, Silas. He said you were never to part with it." "You are your father's own son, and he would be proud."
